heading.en: How does a car turn without skidding?

hook.en: On the ghat road to Chikkamagaluru, cars take sharp bends. Something must pull them towards the centre of each curve: friction, helped by banking the road.
hook.kn: ಚಿಕ್ಕಮಗಳೂರಿನ ಘಾಟ್ ರಸ್ತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾರುಗಳು ತೀಕ್ಷ್ಣ ತಿರುವುಗಳನ್ನು ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ತಿರುವಿನ ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಕಡೆಗೆ ಯಾವುದೋ ಬಲ ಎಳೆಯಬೇಕು: ಅದು ಘರ್ಷಣೆ, ಜೊತೆಗೆ ರಸ್ತೆಯ ಓರೆ.

body.en: A body moving in a circle needs a net *force* $mv^2/R$ towards the centre. On a level road static friction supplies it, so the maximum safe speed is $v_{max} = \sqrt{\mu_s R g}$. Banking the road at angle θ lets the normal reaction help; with no friction at all the ideal speed is $v_0 = \sqrt{Rg\tan\theta}$.
body.kn: ವೃತ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ಚಲಿಸುವ ಕಾಯಕ್ಕೆ ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಕಡೆಗೆ mv²/R ನಿವ್ವಳ ಬಲ ಬೇಕು. ಸಮತಟ್ಟಾದ ರಸ್ತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿರ ಘರ್ಷಣೆ ಅದನ್ನು ಒದಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: v_max = √(μ_s R g). ರಸ್ತೆಯನ್ನು θ ಕೋನದಲ್ಲಿ ಓರೆಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಲಂಬ ಪ್ರತಿಕ್ರಿಯೆಯೂ ನೆರವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: v₀ = √(Rg tanθ).

points.en: *Centripetal force* is not a new kind of force
Banked road with friction: v_max = √[Rg(μ_s + tanθ)/(1 − μ_s tanθ)]

title.en: Banked roads and the Atwood machine

say.en: On a banked road, the normal reaction tilts towards the centre of the curve, and friction helps too.
With no friction, only the normal reaction provides the centripetal force, giving the ideal speed. On a level road, only friction does.
Two masses over a smooth pulley: draw each body separately and apply F equals m a to each.
Add the two equations to find a, then substitute back for the tension.
With 5 and 3 kilograms and g equal to 10, the acceleration is 2.5 and the tension 37.5 newtons.

narration.en: On a curve the car needs a centripetal force mv²/r. A banked road provides part of it from the normal force; friction supplies the rest. At the optimum speed √(rg tan θ) no friction is needed. Above v_max = √(rg(μ + tan θ)/(1 − μ tan θ)) the car skids outwards; far too slow and it slides down the bank.
narration.kn: ತಿರುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾರಿಗೆ mv²/r ಕೇಂದ್ರಾಭಿಮುಖ ಬಲ ಬೇಕು. ಓರೆಯಾದ ರಸ್ತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅದರ ಒಂದು ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಲಂಬ ಬಲ ಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಉಳಿದದ್ದನ್ನು ಘರ್ಷಣೆ. ಆದರ್ಶ ವೇಗ √(rg tan θ) ನಲ್ಲಿ ಘರ್ಷಣೆ ಬೇಡ. v_max ಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದರೆ ಕಾರು ಹೊರಗೆ ಜಾರುತ್ತದೆ; ತುಂಬಾ ನಿಧಾನವಾದರೆ ಇಳಿಜಾರಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಳಗೆ ಜಾರುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Find the maximum speed at which a car can go round a level circular road of radius 50 m if μ_s = 0.2 (g = 10 m/s²).

steps.en: Friction provides the centripetal force: mv²/R ≤ μ_s mg.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the maximum speed at which a car can go round a level circular road of radius 50 m if μ_s = 0.2 (g = 10 m/s²).

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the maximum speed at which a car can go round a level circular road of radius 50 metres if micro _s equals 0.2 (g equals 10 metres per second squared).
Friction provides the centripetal force: mv squared/R is less than or equal to micro _s mg.
v max equals the square root of micro _s R g equals the square root of (0.2 times 50 times 10) equals the square root of 100 equals 10 metres per second.
So the answer is 10 metres per second 36 kilometres per hour.

problem.en: Masses of 3 kg and 2 kg hang from the two ends of a string over a smooth pulley. Find the acceleration and the tension (g = 10 m/s²).

steps.en: Check on the 2 kg mass: T − 20 = 2 × 2, so T = 24 N.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Masses of 3 kg and 2 kg hang from the two ends of a string over a smooth pulley. Find the acceleration and the tension (g = 10 m/s²).

say.en: Let us solve this together. Masses of 3 kilograms and 2 kilograms hang from the two ends of a string over a smooth pulley. Find the acceleration and the tension (g equals 10 metres per second squared).
a equals 3 minus 2 times 10 / 3 plus 2 equals 2 metres per second squared.
T equals 2 times 3 times 2 times 10 divided by 5 equals 24 newtons.
Check on the 2 kilograms mass: T minus 20 equals 2 times 2, so T equals 24 newtons.
So the answer is a equals 2 metres per second squared; T equals 24 newtons.
